proves: A return whose every result is already the zero value of its type has no sbr-zero site: an empty composite literal of a struct or an array, one whose elements are zero values, nil, and the zero value of a type parameter. A return of an empty list is a site, because the list is not nil. A replacement writes each zero value as code does.
fixture: find returns a point and whether it found one, and the zero point when it did not. origin returns zero values only. first returns the first value of a list of any type, or the type's zero value. empty returns an empty list.
